option.approach: Examine whether quasitracial completeness and a valid quantitative order estimate together prove monotone sequential completeness. Establish those ingredients separately rather than assuming that projection completeness supplies them.

options.counterfactual: A finite AW*-factor can contain a bounded increasing self-adjoint sequence with no least upper bound.
options.approach: Check quasitracial completeness independently of order completeness. Determine whether the missing-supremum sequence can be Cauchy in the quasitrace metric without its limit belonging to the original factor.

options.counterfactual: A finite AW*-factor can contain a bounded increasing self-adjoint sequence with no least upper bound.
options.approach: Analyze the quasitracial tail gaps of the sequence. If they stay uniformly positive, use monotone interpolation to obtain exactly equal increments while preserving all upper bounds.

options.counterfactual: A finite AW*-factor can contain a bounded increasing self-adjoint sequence with no least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate whether every missing-supremum sequence must instead have vanishing quasitracial tail gaps. Such a result would explain how G could remain empty despite failure of monotone sequential completeness.

options.counterfactual: There is no universal quantitative estimate controlling the quasitrace distance between ordered positive contractions solely by the difference of their quasitrace values.
options.approach: Replace the single quasitrace-value difference by differences of spectral distribution functions. Investigate whether convergence of those distributions provides enough control to construct a least upper bound.
